CJA Overview

What is Customer Journey Analytics?

Transition into the CJA overview block. Three slides follow: product overview, use cases, and industry applications.

CJA Overview

CJA at a glance

Individual-level customer analysis across every channel, in seconds, built on Adobe Experience Platform.

How it works

Customer Journey Analytics (CJA)
Metrics, dimensions, segments, reports, analyses
▲
Adobe Experience Platform
XDM schema · data lake · identity resolution
▲
Your sources
Web, mobile, survey, call, CRM · streaming or batch

What you get

  • Sequential reports spanning multiple channels
  • Online-to-offline impact analysis
  • Role-based reporting access across the business
  • Ad-hoc, drag-and-drop analysis in Workspace
  • Segments, filters, attribution without re-implementation
Source: ACN deck slide 19. The stack is the point: CJA is a workspace sitting on AEP, which sits on your sources. Data lands from any source, gets organized by XDM, and CJA reads it through a connection, refreshing in as little as an hour. Individual-level and non-web data are the differentiators.

CJA Overview

Key use cases

01
See the customer in a journey context
Analyze data sequentially across channels, including non-web sources, in one reporting view.
02
Make insights available to everyone
Democratize access so anyone responsible for the customer experience can decide faster.
03
Harness data science, without a data scientist
Workspace surfaces deep insight through drag-and-drop; no modeling background required.
04
Control your own data
Create, import, and reshape datasets on demand; Query Service handles extract, transform, and load.
Source: ACN deck slide 20. Keep it brisk; these are familiar. The framing that matters: CJA isn't a better web-analytics tool, it's a different category, built for the whole journey.

CJA Overview

From collection to intelligence

  • Data lands from any source, including SDKs, apps, enterprise systems, and ETL, streaming or batch.
  • Adobe Experience Platform organizes it with XDM and resolves identity in the Real-Time Customer Profile.
  • CJA reads it through a data connection to visualize cross-channel journeys, refreshed in as little as an hour.
Source: ACN deck slide 19 visuals. Walk the left diagram across its three zones (Data Collection, Profile and Data Management, Customer Analysis and Intelligence), then point to the right screenshots as what analysts actually work in. Ties the how-it-works story to the real product.

Architecture

CJA in the context of AEP

Source: ACN deck slide 26. Jonathan leads this block, about 35 minutes. Shift from "what CJA does" to "how it is built on Adobe Experience Platform."

Architecture

How the pieces connect

Datasets are structured in AEP; CJA joins and classifies them for analysis.

Source: ACN deck slide 27. Walk it left to right: a schema shapes a dataset in AEP; one or more datasets join into a connection; a data view classifies those fields into metrics, dimensions, and filters; projects turn that into visualizations. This is the object model the rest of the week builds on.

Architecture

CJA architecture, end to end

Data is ingested into AEP, processed there, then pushed into CJA for analysis.

1 Data sources → 2 Adobe Experience Platform → 3 Connections and data views

Source: ACN deck slide 29. This is the master diagram; the next three slides zoom into each numbered stage. Point out the arrow legend: solid black is ingress, solid red is egress to reporting, dashed is the CJA data flow.

Architecture · Stage 1

Data sources

Every source is first ingested into AEP, by streaming or by batch.

  • Experience Edge Network. Real-time pipeline for immediate personalization; web and mobile interactions.
  • Streaming Data Stores. Continuous streaming for near-real-time analytics, 15 to 60 minute latency; live user behavior.
  • Enterprise Data Stores. Batch files ingested as a single unit; ERP and CRM systems and other cadence-based data.
Source: ACN deck slide 30. The split that matters for this week: Edge and streaming land in minutes; enterprise batch lands on a schedule. That timing difference is why some data appears later than the rest.

Architecture · Stage 2

Adobe Experience Platform

Once ingested, data is processed inside AEP.

  • Real-Time Customer Profile. Identity resolves a customer across channels; Profile is the aggregated view; Segments are dynamic audiences.
  • Data Ingestion. Batch for scheduled, large-volume imports; Stream for real-time capture.
  • Data Lake. Governance keeps data quality and compliance; Query Service provides flexible, scalable querying.
Source: ACN deck slide 31. Identity resolution in the Real-Time Customer Profile is the piece that turns fragmented touchpoints into one person; call it out.

Architecture · Stage 3

Connections and data views

Finally, data is pushed from AEP into CJA.

  • Connection. Integrates one or more AEP datasets into Workspace.
  • Data View. Determines how you interpret the data from a connection.
  • Projects. Where you build analyses to gather insights.
Source: ACN deck slide 32. This is where the week lives: connections and data views on Thursday, projects and analysis throughout. Everything upstream exists to make this step possible.

Architecture

Zooming out: CJA is one part of Adobe Experience Platform

Customer Journey Analytics is a single application on the platform (highlighted). The same data, identities, and audiences also feed Real-Time CDP, Journey Optimizer, Target, and the rest.
The zoom-out. CJA reads from the same Experience Platform that powers activation and engagement, which is why the architecture we just covered matters beyond reporting: the data foundation is shared. An orientation slide, so keep it brief.

A Sample Journey

Questions we can ask about this journey

1What percent of members move through each phase of the journey, and where do they drop off?
2Which email nudges are most effective at driving members to complete registration?
3Do members who answer more of the Health Interest Survey (one answer vs. three vs. four) engage differently in the Guided Member Welcome?
4At which Guided Member Welcome steps do members turn to the call center?
5For members who reach the call center, does a low satisfaction rating predict whether they finish onboarding?
6Which post-onboarding engagement campaigns bring back members who stalled in the Guided Member Welcome?
Tie each question back to the journey they just saw. Every one needs data from more than one source, stitched to a single member, which is exactly what CJA does and what the rest of the week builds toward. Revisit these on Thursday against real data.

3. What does a data view do?
a) Physically moves data between systems · b) Specifies how data from a connection is interpreted (metrics, dimensions, session settings) · c) Builds the identity graph used to stitch profiles · d) Stores the raw datasets in Adobe Experience Platform

a) It defines the metrics and dimensions of a report · b) It stitches identities together · c) It brings one or more Adobe Experience Platform datasets into CJA · d) It sends audiences out for activation

a) Analysis Workspace · b) The Data Lake · c) Data Prep · d) The Experience Edge Network

a) Data views · b) Analysis Workspace · c) Query Service · d) The Experience Edge Network

Data collection

Create Your Own Journeys

New chapter and the shift into the afternoon: participants stop watching and start generating their own journey data across the channels. The channel assets and hands-on labs slot in after this.

Data collection

A journey is a sequence of events, for a given person, spread over time.
events = what happened a given person = who over time = when
The one-line definition that anchors the build. A journey is just events for one person over time, which is exactly the who, when, and what on the next slides. Everything participants generate this afternoon adds events to a person's journey.

Data collection

An event is just who, when, and what

The data you'll generate is a stream of events. Each one captures three things:

👤 Who
Person identifier
🕒 When
Timestamp
⚡ What
The event
4f2a-9c71Jan 14, 9:14 AM🌐Viewed the home page
4f2a-9c71Jan 14, 9:22 AM📋Completed a survey
b83e-1d40Jan 16, 2:47 PM📞Called the support line
4f2a-9c71Jan 18, 7:05 PM🛒Purchased a product
c5a7-77e2Jan 21, 10:31 AM🌐Viewed the home page
b83e-1d40Jan 22, 8:15 AM📋Completed a survey
That is all an event is. A page view, a survey, a phone call, each becomes one row like these. Generating your journey means creating events like these.
Sets the frame for the exercises. Keep it concrete: an event is who did something, when, and what. Note that the same person (4f2a-9c71) shows up across several events over time, which is exactly the stream each participant will build for their persona.

Data collection

The Who: one person, many identities

The same member is captured under several identity namespaces. The identity graph links them back into one person.

👤 Who = identities across namespaces
The same person, seen under different namespaces:
ECID82911744027735…
GUID4f2a-9c71-b0e8…
Member ID60482
App user ID3391
Email (hashed)9c8f1a…
Each line is a link, formed when two identities appear together on the same event, such as a login, a registration, or an app sign-in. Connected identities resolve to one person, which is what makes cross-channel analysis possible.
The identity graph is the engine behind stitching. Nodes are identifiers; an edge forms when two identifiers show up on the same event. Point out that this cluster is one person even though no single system holds all five IDs.

Data collection

The When: the event's timestamp

One value per event: exactly when it happened.

🕒 timestamp
2026-01-18T19:05:00Z
Jan 18, 2026 · 7:05 PM
Recorded in ISO 8601. It is what puts events in order and lets you follow a journey over time.
The simplest of the three. Every event carries a timestamp, stored in ISO 8601 (not Unix epoch in CJA and AEP). It is what turns a set of events into a sequence, the "over time" part of the journey definition.

Data collection

The schema defines these fields and organizes them into logical groups. On the left, the fields as name-value pairs; on the right, the schema itself.

A simplified XDM schema for one event, tied to the purchase. Field groups (Identity, Web, Commerce) organize the fields, and each carries a value. This is the bridge to components: dimensions and metrics are built from these fields.

Data collection

From a source into Experience Platform

The events you generate are sent by a source, like the website, to Adobe Experience Platform. There, a schema checks their structure and a dataset stores them.

The schema is the contract for the data; the dataset is where matching events land. Same flow we saw in the architecture, now for your own events.
A light bridge from events to the platform. Keep it quick, the architecture was covered earlier. The point that matters for the lab: an event travels source to schema to dataset, and those are the objects they will go find.

Data collection

Identities and the profile store

As events arrive, AEP links their identities and assembles one profile per person in the Real-Time Customer Profile, the profile store.

Linked identities
ECID, GUID, Member ID…

Data collection

Meet the journey simulator

We've stood up a website where you create a member persona and walk the New Member Welcome journey as them. Every step generates real event data you can inspect.

  • Create a persona and move through the journey: enroll, register, survey, call.
  • Web steps fire real events; you can see the ECID, GUID, and XDM payload live.
  • Backend steps, like the membership record and Marketo sends, generate their own data.
  • Each step has a data source, so you can tie the raw data back to this morning's event concepts.

⚠ Site build in progress. Drop in the URL when ready: [persona site URL]

Introduce the tool that makes the morning concrete. Skeleton for now; the site, personas, and per-step data sources are being built. The promise: click a step, see the exact event you just created.

Data collection · Watch

Watch: one persona, end to end

A presenter walks a sample persona through the whole journey and calls out what is happening under the hood.

  • The ECID and XDM payload as each web step fires, live in the Experience Platform Debugger.
  • How logging in ties the anonymous ECID to the Member ID.
  • The backend membership record and Marketo send events.
  • The support call, with its transcript and sentiment (we come back to this on Day 4).

⚠ Presenter demo, pending the live site.

The "I do." One presenter drives a sample persona while everyone watches, narrating ECID, payload, the login stitch, backend events, and the call transcript. Seeds the Day 4 sentiment and derived-field tie-in. Use the Experience Platform Debugger or Assurance.

Data collection · Hands-on

Together: find your ECID

Before the full lab, everyone does one step and finds their own ECID.

  1. Open the [persona site] and start your persona's first web step.
  2. Open the Experience Platform Debugger and find your ECID in the payload.
The "we do." One guided step so everyone succeeds once before going independent. It de-risks the long lab and makes the ECID real. Confirm each person is on their own browser profile so IDs do not collide.

Hands-on · Lab

Lab: generate your journey

Now you drive. Take your persona card and complete every step of the journey.

  • Use your [persona card]: name, region, plan, identifiers, and the steps to perform.
  • Complete each step: enroll, register, health survey, select PCP, support call, mobile.
  • Capture your ECID, GUID, and Member ID as you go.
  • The call step records a transcript; we classify it for sentiment on Day 4.

⚠ Persona cards and steps to be finalized with the site.

The long lab, roughly 45 minutes. Persona cards are the spec, so the data is predictable and IDs do not collide. Data flows to AEP; because of batch latency, the stitched result is inspected as Day 2's opener rather than live. Keep a pre-generated dataset ready in case live generation stalls.

Data collection

When your data shows up

Your events do not all arrive at once.

  • Web, mobile, and call events: streaming, they land in minutes.
  • Membership, survey, and Marketo: batch, they land overnight.
  • The stitched, cross-channel result is where Day 2 begins.
This is the batch-latency lesson from this morning, now with your own data. Tomorrow you open Workspace and find your journey, stitched into one person.
Closes the section and bridges to Day 2. Set the expectation that not everything is visible immediately, which is realistic and is the batch-latency concept in action.
